idiom_name: plain object literals with dynamic property access
implementation_notes: JavaScript objects already are loosely typed, dynamically composed property maps, so the document half of the pattern disappears: bracket access reads keys that are only known at runtime, JSON.parse produces the tree, and getters, Object.defineProperty or a Proxy cover computed and validated property access. Only the typed-view half remains, and the language offers nothing for it at runtime - views live in JSDoc annotations or a TypeScript declaration, or are written as explicit accessor functions plus runtime guards. Keep property shapes stable for the engine's benefit: adding keys later is fine, but mixing types and deleting properties degrades hidden-class performance.
pitfalls: Bracket access with a key from external input can reach Object.prototype members (constructor, __proto__), enabling prototype pollution or injection; use Object.hasOwn or a null-prototype/Map-based document.
Deleting properties or storing many differently typed values defeats the engine's shape assumptions, so the map stays cheap only while it stays monomorphic.
Nothing is enforced: a renamed or mistyped key is an undefined that propagates silently until far away code fails.
Using Object.hasOwn only for reads but copying attacker-controlled keys with Object.assign can still trigger prototype setters; validate allowed keys and merge into a null-prototype object or Map.
